root.claim: Exact multiplication of two $n$-bit integers runs in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ time on one deterministic fixed-tape machine, with $\kappa = 2^{-182}$.
root.method: reduce exact multiplication to radix-digit convolution, compute that convolution with fast tape transforms, and recover the exact product

motivation.text: Linear combinations of intermediate data cut the cost of both address rearrangement and transform layers, which the fixed-tape bound needs.

quote.quote: The algorithm uses linear combinations of intermediate data to reduce the cost of both address rearrangement and Fourier-transform layers

root.salient: A strict power saving in the logarithmic factor, valid for every input length.

adds.name: input width
adds.meaning: The number of bits in each of the two input integers.

adds.name: saving exponent
adds.meaning: The fixed constant $2^{-182}$ that makes the logarithmic factor a power below $\lg n$.
